subjects: any subject taught with flat 2D diagrams
measured_on: 37 Indian-economy reference videos for UPSC (about 4 h 35 min): batch 2 (20 videos, 27 Oct 2026) and batch 3 (17 videos, 4 Nov 2026). Visual change events by code (events.py, 5 fps frame differences), speech phrases by Silero VAD (vad_sync.py), 346 teaching segments carded with the v3 fields (cards/, aggregate3.py).

measurements.canvas_clears_per_video: about 1 (most videos are 1 to 3 canvases, re-framed by zooms about 7 times per video)
measurements.visual_level: L2 in almost every segment (flat 2D); no L3 world in any of the 37

rules.rule: One canvas per idea: build it piece by piece instead of cutting to a new shot every sentence. Clear the canvas only when the idea changes; otherwise re-frame with a zoom or pan to the part being explained.
rules.check: code: canvas plan per part; camera keys instead of new scenes

rules.rule: Something on the canvas changes about every 5 s (one change per one or two spoken phrases).
The picture never stays the same for more than 15 s (the references sometimes hold 40-80 s; BIE must not).
A new element appears on its own word, while it is being said (about 40% into the phrase, never in the pause after).
rules.check: code: every element has a cue word found in its beat (timing.cue_frame)

rules.rule: Numbers that change are struck out and replaced on screen (50 -> 65), with an up/down arrow, on the word of the new number.
Many people/things are shown as a crowd that grows or shrinks with the story (2 buyers -> 12 -> 3).
A running numeric example carries the concept (price 50 -> 65, GDP 10K -> 11K -> 12.1K at 10%).
rules.check: director: every concept part names its example numbers

rules.rule: Return to the topic tree and tick the branch that is done before starting the next branch.
rules.check: director: recap step after each branch

rules.rule: One anchor diagram stays (a band, a tree, a rate card) while the part beside or below it changes.
rules.check: director: anchor element with long life; layout keeps its cells

rules.rule: No overlap, nothing outside the safe area, captions strip kept clear, readable text (>= 24 px at 1080p), at most 16 elements on screen.
No photos or caricatures of real people, no logos, emblems or regulator marks: use a name card, a generic icon or BIE's own presenter character.
rules.check: code: icons only from the CC BY index (no brands); director vocabulary has no photo kind

rules.rule: Light paper theme for build-up canvases (dark theme stays for 3D/science worlds); subtitles on a dark strip.

Show, do not write: every mechanism, process and cause-effect line is carried by things acting (a pattern from rules/show_lexicon.json), not by a sentence box. The references manage this in only 11% of segments; BIE's target is every such line.
rules.check: director: each beat names a show-lexicon pattern; LOOK review counts said = shown

rules.rule: Words on screen stay low: a term pill, a number, a short label; about 25 words at most on screen at once and no sentence box for more than 10 s (the references reach a median of 38 and a p90 of 90 words).
rules.check: code: words on screen per frame; sentence-box lifetime

rules.rule: Reuse the same picture to show a change or a contrast (same store for three causes of inflation; BPLR picture reused for base rate with the arrows flipped); only the part that changes moves.
Follow one object through a calculation or a chain (one egg through the price index; one bond through its owners).
rules.check: director: numbers/formula beats name the followed object

rules.rule: Institutions are shown by institutionBadge or a generic building with a name plate; never a logo, emblem, seal, real landmark or real person (the references show logos in 25 of 37 videos).
rules.check: code: no brand or photo assets; saanche only

rules.rule: A reference video is evidence for showing, never for facts: numbers, dates and laws come from the book and are checked (several reference claims were doubtful).
rules.check: code: every on-screen number and date traces to a book item

batch3_changes: 4 Nov 2026: measurements re-done on 37 videos (the batch-3 numbers matched batch 2 within 0.6 s); rules CV-13 to CV-18 added from the v3 cards and the Money v2 verdict.
